## India: DPDPA Implementation and Challenges

The Supreme Court has sought a response from the Centre regarding petitions filed by media associations challenging the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), arguing it infringes on press freedom. While MeitY Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw reiterated that the Act does not undermine journalistic liberty, the government remains open to media suggestions for amendments.

The government has issued a "Removal of Difficulties Order 2026" for the DPDPA, aiming to clarify certain implementation aspects. Meanwhile, organizations like OneConsent and PHDCCI are collaborating to help Indian businesses achieve DPDPA compliance, highlighting the ongoing efforts to prepare various sectors for the new regime, including educational institutions.
